qualifying_updates.title: SkillHone discussion frames agent skills as maintained decision history, not static prompt files
qualifying_updates.factual_summary: The article discusses the July 2026 SkillHone paper and argues that teams should preserve the decisions behind agent skill changes, not only the latest SKILL.md. It connects skill maintenance to changing APIs, repository conventions, sharper evals, security rules, and recurring workflow failures.
qualifying_updates.why_it_matters_for_ai_assisted_developme: Durable agent instructions need provenance and change rationale. Local prompt-and-instructions and context-architecture guidance should treat skills as maintained runbooks with decision history, exit criteria, and verification evidence.
qualifying_updates.follow_up_notes: Potential ingest destination: prompt-and-instructions/rules-and-knowledge-layers.md or context-architecture/context-state-externalization-and-rehydration.md. Keep SkillHone background upstream-owned.

qualifying_updates.title: Kodem lists MCP security controls around least privilege, argument validation, sandboxing, approvals, and runtime monitoring
qualifying_updates.factual_summary: Kodem describes MCP security as constraining what each MCP connection can do and watching it at runtime. The page names indirect prompt injection through tool content, over-privileged tools, unvalidated tool arguments, untrusted servers, token exposure, least privilege, sandboxing, confirmation gates, and runtime observation of tool calls and side effects.
qualifying_updates.why_it_matters_for_ai_assisted_developme: MCP is upstream-owned as a protocol, but the local practice implication is concrete: tool-call governance should include capability scoping, policy validation before execution, untrusted-tool-output handling, approval gates, and runtime audit evidence.

qualifying_updates.title: CodeRabbit changelog adds git-history secret scanning, PR file limits, and in-app review conversation handling
qualifying_updates.factual_summary: CodeRabbit listed July 15 updates for opt-in repository-history secret scanning, plan-specific automatic PR review file limits, usage-priced on-demand review continuation within the 300-file ceiling, and in-app handling of grouped review threads with resolved or outdated state.
qualifying_updates.why_it_matters_for_ai_assisted_developme: AI code review is gaining explicit capacity limits, cost gates, and security-history coverage. Local code-review practice should treat large PRs as a budgeted review workflow and separate current-code findings from repository-history secret risk.

qualifying_updates.title: WorkOS highlights MCP interceptors as a draft policy-and-evidence layer for agent tool permissions
qualifying_updates.factual_summary: WorkOS describes the still-draft SEP-1763 Interceptor Framework for MCP as a pattern for deciding what agents are allowed to do and what evidence exists afterward. The article frames interceptors as a cross-server control point for PII redaction, audit logging, rate limiting, and validation against prompt injection.
qualifying_updates.why_it_matters_for_ai_assisted_developme: The local practice implication is that MCP governance should avoid server-by-server policy drift. Teams need a common interception layer for policy enforcement, audit evidence, and pre-tool-call validation across heterogeneous agent tools.
named_entities: Interceptor Framework for Model Context Protocol
qualifying_updates.follow_up_notes: Potential ingest destination: retrieval-and-tools/tool-call-and-mcp-governance.md and application-patterns/agent-harness-components.md. Treat SEP background as upstream-owned.

qualifying_updates.title: Shiplight updates a coding-agent context-engineering guide around instructions, repo knowledge, tool results, tests, and runtime feedback
qualifying_updates.factual_summary: Shiplight defines context engineering for coding agents as deciding which tokens an agent sees at each change-generation step, including instructions, repository knowledge, tool results, tests, and feedback from running code. The guide distinguishes coding-agent context loops from one-shot prompt engineering.
qualifying_updates.why_it_matters_for_ai_assisted_developme: The guide reinforces local context-architecture coverage: the context contract should be curated per loop step and should privilege executable feedback, tests, and source evidence over bulk context loading.

qualifying_updates.title: LangChain argues agents need isolated, disposable computers for safe execution loops
qualifying_updates.factual_summary: LangChain says agents need real execution environments with a filesystem, shell, package manager, network access, and step-persistent state to run code, inspect results, and retry. It argues production systems need isolated, disposable environments because agent-executed code may be generated mid-loop, influenced by user input, cloned repositories, packages, or web documents, and may not have been reviewed before execution.
qualifying_updates.why_it_matters_for_ai_assisted_developme: This maps directly to agent harness architecture: coding agents need execution access to verify work, but that access should live in isolated workspaces separated from user laptops, production systems, and other agents.

qualifying_updates.title: Atlassian analysis places context and governance ahead of agents for AI-native software delivery
qualifying_updates.factual_summary: The article reports Atlassian's emphasis on a Teamwork Graph context layer that maps work, code, people, decisions, dependencies, tasks, requirements, conversations, code context, and customer insight. The quoted framing says the context layer requires retrieving only relevant, current information and that agents fail when everything is thrown together.
qualifying_updates.why_it_matters_for_ai_assisted_developme: The local implication is not Atlassian product coverage but practice design: agentic software delivery needs context graphs, freshness controls, and governance before assigning work to agents.

qualifying_updates.title: Caddi frames loop engineering as act-observe-decide-stop design for reliable multi-step AI work
qualifying_updates.factual_summary: Caddi distinguishes prompt engineering, context engineering, and loop engineering. It defines the loop as acting, observing results, deciding the next move or retry, and stopping when work is complete, arguing that production AI must handle messy inputs repeatedly without constant human watching.
qualifying_updates.why_it_matters_for_ai_assisted_developme: The loop framing is useful for coding-agent planning and verification: local guidance should require explicit observe/retry/stop conditions, not just prompts and context bundles.

qualifying_updates.title: Check Point AI security coverage highlights malicious durable instruction files and AI-accelerated patch bottlenecks
qualifying_updates.source_type: dated security news based on vendor report
qualifying_updates.factual_summary: Help Net Security summarizes Check Point's AI Security Report 2026. It says attackers can target coding agents by planting malicious instructions in files such as CLAUDE.md that load automatically at session start, and notes that AI can accelerate vulnerability discovery and exploit development until patch testing and deployment become the bottleneck.
qualifying_updates.why_it_matters_for_ai_assisted_developme: Local practice should treat durable agent instruction files as an attack surface and require review gates for repository-loaded instructions. Regression repair and patch workflows also need speed without skipping validation, because exploit timelines are compressing.

qualifying_updates.title: Cast AI launches Kimchi Coding GA with multi-model routing, spend caps, loop termination, and data-sovereignty claims
qualifying_updates.factual_summary: Cast AI announced general availability for Kimchi Coding, describing it as an autonomous multi-model coding agent with task routing by complexity and cost, feedback loops that score generated code, hard spend caps from API keys to organizations, automatic termination for runaway loops, a FinOps dashboard, and deployment options including customer VPC, dedicated GPUs, and air-gapped environments.
qualifying_updates.why_it_matters_for_ai_assisted_developme: The product and vendor are upstream-owned, but the local practice signal is that cost governance, model routing, loop termination, and data-residency controls are becoming first-class coding-agent harness requirements.
